---
title: Adaptive highlight pair (github / arrow)
format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: cosmo
      dark: darkly
highlight-style:
  light: github
  dark: arrow
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      dom-parity: true
      # The whole point: both palette names are Q1 built-ins that the
      # .theme translator now ships, so the render is warning-free
      # (regression guard for the Q-14-5 fallback both names used to
      # trigger — bd-hl-theme-translator-2mdgh4k6).
      noErrorsOrWarnings: true
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - [!str 'hl-keyword">def</span>']
      ensureCssRegexMatches:
        # github-light keyword red in the light stylesheet and
        # arrow-dark keyword salmon in the dark one (both stylesheets
        # are linked, so the combined CSS carries both), plus
        # github-light's translated code-block canvas.
        - ["\\.hl-keyword", "#d73a49", "#ffa07a"]
        # Neither variant may fall back to the default palette's
        # solarized keyword green.
        - ["#859900"]
---

The ordinary Quarto 1 adaptive pairing: `light: github` resolves to the
`github-light` palette, `dark: arrow` to `arrow-dark`, each translated
from its vendored `.theme` file onto the `hl-*` class vocabulary.

```python
def hello():
    print("Hello, World!")
```
